title: Tartiflette
subtitle: Savoyard gratin of potatoes, lardons, and Reblochon
excerpt: A thick, hearty gratin from the French Alps: potatoes layered with sautéed onion and lardons, bathed in white wine and cream, then topped with a whole Reblochon cheese and baked until molten and golden.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tartiflette is from the Savoie region of the French Alps, where it was created in the 1980s as a promotional dish for Reblochon, the local soft washed-rind cheese. Despite its recent invention, it draws on much older Alpine traditions of cooking potatoes with cheese and cured pork. It became one of the most popular après-ski dishes in France and spread internationally through ski resorts in the 1990s. Reblochon is a protected-origin cheese from the Haute-Savoie; if unavailable, Brie or Camembert can be substituted, though the flavour will differ.

content.text: Par-boil the potatoes rather than roasting them from raw: the dish needs only 25 to 30 minutes in the oven to melt the cheese, which is not long enough to cook raw potato slices through. Slice the potatoes about 5 mm thick once par-boiled. The Reblochon goes on top cut-side down for the last part of baking so the rind does not prevent the interior from melting. If you cannot find Reblochon, use Brie and accept a different but still delicious result.
Par-boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 12 to 15 minutes until just tender. Drain and allow to cool slightly. Slice into 5 mm rounds.

Fry the lardons in the butter in a wide pan for 4 minutes until golden. Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and thyme and stir for 1 minute. Add the white wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Season. Remove from the heat.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Butter a baking dish. Layer half the potato slices in the base. Spoon half the lardon mixture over. Repeat with the remaining potato and lardon mixture. Pour the cream over the top.

Place the Reblochon halves cut-side down on top of the dish. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the cheese is melted and the top is golden and bubbling. Serve from the dish with a green salad and cornichons.
